issue_context.title: `SkipWaitToCompletion` semantics in scheduler performance test framework
issue_context.body:
`SkipWaitToCompletion` is a very useful option in scheduler perf test framework to define an operation without waiting for it to finish. However, the current testing logic still waits for all the pods in this operation to be schedulable, in the last step:

- [Record](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5144e2ec78ccd1ae6ab77075d88604159b957bfa/test/integration/scheduler_perf/scheduler_perf_test.go#L366-L373) the `Count` number  
- [Wait](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5144e2ec78ccd1ae6ab77075d88604159b957bfa/test/integration/scheduler_perf/scheduler_perf_test.go#L414) for Pods in this operation to be schedulable

This can be problematic as some case just want to generate [unschedulable](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6d43e2b3bb55237fbb64118dc13beac259745983/test/integration/scheduler_perf/config/performance-config.yaml#L424) Pods (for example, to test internal queuing or sorting behavior/latency). The following test command times out as those large-cpu Pods are expected to not fit on any node:

```
make test-integration WHAT=./test/integration/scheduler_perf KUBE_TEST_VMODULE="''" KUBE_TEST_ARGS="-alsologtostderr=false -logtostderr=false -run=^$$ -benchtime=1ns -bench=BenchmarkPerfScheduling/Unschedulable/500Nodes/200InitPods/1000PodsToSchedule"
```

So, given `SkipWaitToCompletion` is commented as:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5144e2ec78ccd1ae6ab77075d88604159b957bfa/test/integration/scheduler_perf/scheduler_perf_test.go#L215-L217

I'm proposing to relax the semantics to not wait for the Pods to be schedulable if the operation is specified as `SkipWaitToCompletion`.

/sig scheduling

review_comments:
I am not quite understanding what's the actual meaning of this `Op`, this `Op` must be explicitly set in the template, give a `skipWaitToCompletion` defined to `true` without the `Op` doesn't bring us anything, e.g. the `Unschedulable` benchmark, what am I missing? @adtac 
```
// A barrierOp is added at the end of each each workload automatically.
```

>the test will be crashed always, see code at line 385

yes, we shouldn't remove the `numPodsScheduledPerNamespace` segment. Instead, the real problem seems to be this, as @chendave pointed out:

>// A barrierOp is added at the end of each each workload automatically.

The `waitUntilPodsScheduled` call at the end of the `runWorkload` function seems to the root cause of this bug and it should be removed. I had incorrectly assumed that all must be scheduled at the end of the workload.

Thanks @chendave and @adtac. +1 to remove the assumption that each workload needs to be followed by a `waitUntilPodsScheduled`.

So closing this issue in favor of #98721.
